factChecks: Every numeric key the rewrite wrote or kept is recomputed from its arithmetic in packages/curriculum/tests/psychology-how-minds-work-v2.test.ts, which passes; the full curriculum, server and web suites and the typecheck passed when this record was written.

The migration apply step ran the v2 validator and the publication lesson rules with 0 errors: vocabulary order, skill scope, a response on every practice screen, a transfer, three skill-check items, citations on every step, question and flashcard. Every warning is accepted below with its reason.
Writing agents' reports: numeric keys recomputed, existing question ids kept so learner history still resolves.

Lead's reading was a sample only: the first lesson of Biology, Philosophy and Maths Foundations was read in full, and Astronomy lesson 1 was checked against the approved prototype. Every other lesson was read by its writing agent and checked by the validator, not by the lead.

Not played in a browser by George or any learner. Drawn figures (svg_figure) were added by Claude Sonnet 5.5 agents, who rendered and looked at each one in both themes; the run was stopped part-way, so later lessons still have none and the rest are listed under .authoring/figure-wishlist.md. Every drawing passes the svg_figure safety gate. The lead did not look at the drawings.
Course introduction added (course.introduction), written by the lesson agents from the course description and module list.

Curriculum-first rewrite (2026-11-01): every lesson re-authored from its objective by a Claude Sonnet agent to the discere-lesson-voice skill (voice B); 99 question ids reused, 3 new. Sources were unreachable from the authoring session; the agent softened claims it could not support (power-posing replication no longer called preregistered, illustrative figures labelled as such) and listed the study details it wrote from memory (Jacowitz and Kahneman, Darley and Latané 85/62/31%, Burger 70% vs 82.5%, Hagger et al. 23 labs and d about 0.6, Perry, Doyen et al., Ranehill et al. n = 200). The lead (Claude Opus) checked each against its own knowledge, not against the sources; packages/curriculum/tests/psychology-content.test.ts recomputes the numeric keys. George has not yet read the course.

Opener sentences that announced the lesson were deleted or rewritten as statements about the subject (voice skill: an opener never lists what the lesson covers). Only intro.hook text changed; questions, answers and figures are unchanged.
Fix pass: introduction, openers, question leads and types
Choice options reordered so the correct one is not usually first
Giveaway pass: no answer printed before its question
Screens no longer refer to a figure they do not have
Teaching-screen headlines replaced with short topic titles written by hand; lesson text, questions and figures unchanged.

Teaching screens trimmed so length follows how hard each idea is: restatements, figure narration and previews cut, hard screens kept whole; defined terms, numbers and figure instructions preserved by script, and question facts checked against the new text.

Full learner read of every lesson: restored context the trim cut, corrected facts, arithmetic, reveals, hints and feedback that did not match their questions, removed giveaways, fixed formatting and stale hover notes.
Question review: formats judged against their purpose, free text and faded examples fixed

November 2026 marking fixes: numeric tolerances matched to the rounding each prompt asks for, typed card backs made to contain the expected term, and the listed errors from docs/holistic-review-2026-11.md corrected. Changed numbers were recomputed; no other facts were rechecked.
Source records checked on 2026-11-11: each address was requested and its page compared with the record, and the outcome is recorded on the source as 'checked'. No teaching content changed.

Question rewrite (2026-11-13), following docs/question-writing-guide.md and adapted to an empirical science: 105 questions asked, 147 before. 44 have new ids, 2 unused questions were rewritten in place and are now asked, 59 were kept (37 of them given a second hint), and 86 were deleted: the 42 that no lesson asked and 44 that were replaced. Numeric questions fell from 79 to 14, kept only where the number is the point (an effect size, a replication, a base-rate count, a rate gap). Seven questions put a public-domain classic in front of the learner in the question's extracts, each quoted word for word from the page named in its source record and matched by script (Darwin's queries, William James on selective interest and on perception, Ebbinghaus on the forgetting curve in two questions, Thorndike's law of effect, Le Bon on crowds), and one sets two Ebbinghaus passages side by side. Seven sort and two order questions replace multiple-choice questions that tested one pair. Seven review cards that drilled arithmetic were replaced. Recomputed: every kept numeric key, and the figures stated in the new feedback, in packages/curriculum/tests/psychology-how-minds-work-v2.test.ts. Not checked: no source was read beyond the extract and the abstracts the lessons already cite, the lesson prose was not reread, the 36 questions inside the three course checks were not changed, and nothing was played in a browser.
Option lengths balanced: wrong answer options lengthened so the right option is not the longest. No facts changed.
